newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican TV shows crowd burning man to death.
newsitem.headline: Mexican TV shows crowd burning man to death.

text.p: Mexican television news programmes on Wednesday showed startling images of a bloodied and beaten man being burnt to death by a crowd.
The man, Rodolfo Solar Hernandez, in his late 20s, was alleged to have raped and killed a young woman.
He was killed by an informal committee of residents in a small town near the border of the southern states of Oaxaca and Veracruz.
Mexico's largest televison channel Televisa broadcast a video of the incident on its main news programme, 24 Hours, as did the second largest channel, TV Azteca.
After being badly beaten and tied to a tree, the townspeople poured gasoline over the man, then lit him on fire.
As flames overwhelmed the man, he screamed several times. The video then showed a charred corpse, with smoke rising from the twitching body.
The townspeople decided to judge the man themselves and took a poll.
"The people decided. Everyone signed this," said one middle-aged man, who was unidentified but spoke directly into the camera as he waved a piece of paper.
Officials in the state of Veracruz have started an investigation, the televison programme 24 Hours said.
The incident follows other similar attacks reported recently in Mexico.
Earlier this week, television news programmes showed the blackened corpses of two people lynched and burnt to death in the southern state of Chiapas.
Another lynching took place in the state of Oaxaca last weekend.
